Pro:

- Evaluation is carried on 5 databases with good results.
- Most of the appendixes are informative 

Cons:
 - (minor) The paper cites a lot of prior work in the first paragraph and few have relevance for the topic. I do not see the point of listing many methods without discussing them or using them in comparison, especially old ones.
 - (medium) The review  (Laurentini & Bottino, 2014) does not provide evidence that "Facial Beauty (FB) has a great impact on career development, interpersonal relationships, social status and social acceptance". Some of the papers cited there might provide such evidence, but anyway this is a strong phrase and it should be motivated carefully

Currently my understanding is that this paper is a combination of those two.

For SCUT-FBP5500, it appears that one of the five folds was used as test and the rest as training (for all databases, yet this is not quite explained). content.title: Response to Reviewer 6B4M Part 1
content.comment:
Thanks for your comment. The responses to the comments are listed one by one below, the revision has been highlighted in **green** color. Because of the character limit, we will divide the response into multiple parts.

**Q1. The paper cites a lot of prior work in the first paragraph, and few have relevance to the topic. I do not see the point of listing many methods without discussing them or using them in comparison, especially old ones.**

A1: Completeness of related workers has been considered an important aspect of evaluating a research paper. Therefore, we reviewed most works on the FBP task, even if they are old.  

We only compare with the recent methods because they demonstrated better performances than old ones. In this work, our UOL outperforms these recent methods, which indicates UOL can outperform old ones as well. Therefore, we did not list the comparison with old methods in the paper. 

**Q2. The review (Laurentini & Bottino, 2014) does not provide evidence that "Facial Beauty (FB) has a great impact on career development, interpersonal relationships, social status and social acceptance". Some of the papers cited there might provide such evidence, but anyway, this is a strong phrase and it should be motivated carefully.**

A2: Laurentini & Bottino's paper has the following description on page 2, lines 45 - 58:

_In any case, from ancient Greek culture to our times, no one denied the strong influence of beauty on human life. A number of recent studies, as well as everyday common experience, show that face and body harmony is extremely important in general social life. In a society that is virtually obsessed by beauty, looking unpleasant or different can deeply affect self-esteem and result in social isolation, depression and serious psychological disorders. Attractive people are also likely to be regarded as better than unattractive people in a broad social sense. For instance, experimental research shows that better-looking candidates are more likely to be hired than equally qualified but less attractive people. Thus, it is not surprising that more money is spent annually in the US on beauty related items or services than on both education and social services._

We think their study claims that FB has a great impact on career development, interpersonal relationships and social status.

**Q3. pg. 1 near the bottom "Even FB scores across different datasets are normalized to the same scale, obvious biases still exist, as shown in Fig. 1 (a)" Figure 1 shows that there is no unanimity while human observers labeled facial beauty. Nothing about the bias. In particular in fig (a) it is not clear to me what one should observe!?**

A3: Actually, three datasets have varied FB score ranges. Figure 1(a) illustrates that even though the scores of the three datasets are normalized to the same range, facial images with the same score still have different FB appearances. “bias” means that the FB appearances are inconsistent. Most volunteers in our experiments ranked the right face as the most beautiful one, and the left face as the second one. 

**Q4. The paper should have discussed different aspects with respect to prior works (Lin et al 2022; F.Bougourzi et al 2022 Knowledge-Based Systems) in more detail. These papers are too close to the proposed method: the first one uses ranking to learn beauty prediction, while the second removes outliers and goes for statistical fit too. Currently, my understanding is that this paper is a combination of those two.**

A4: The methods proposed by Lin et al. and F. Bougourzi et al. are good but different from our UOL. We disagree that our work is a combination of the two. The differences are the following.

Although R3CNN (Lin et al.) considers relative ranking, it aims to train a better regression model. Essentially, R3CNN still learns a one-to-one mapping between a facial image and a FB score. Instead, our UOL learns the relative order between images. Moreover, UOL also learns a relationship "$\approx$" which denotes the FB appearances of two images are indistinguishable. But, Lin et al.'s work has no such a relation.

Similarly, the method proposed by F. Bougourzi et al. also aims to train a better regression model. They apply dynamic loss parameters to minimize the effect of outliers, which is very different from our uncertainty modeling. They use the variance of multiple ratings to compute the ϵ-error metric other than training networks to model the multiple ratings.

content.title: Response to Reviewer 6B4M Part 2
content.comment:
**Q5. The evaluation section is not so strong. For SCUT-FBP5500, it appears that one of the five folds was used as a test and the rest as training (for all databases, yet this is not quite explained). Not all cited works report results for all the databases mentioned here. Therefore, I assumed that, for those papers, author-released code has been used (yet this is also not clarified - especially if multiple training or a unique one was used). It seems to me that a unique solution has been used for all databases, and given that most previous works are rather old, the claim of better fitting w.r.t to domain shift is not well argued Also here F.Bougourzi et al 2022 "Deep learning based face beauty prediction via dynamic robust losses and ensemble regression" Knowledge-Based Systems reports slightly better results on SCUT-FBP database.**

A5: We followed previous works and carried out 5-fold cross-validation on the SCUT-FBP5500 dataset, and report the average result of 5 trials. Specifically, each method has five trained versions. For other methods, we listed their results if their papers reported, otherwise, we carried out a 5-fold test on datasets and reported the average result. As this work aims at a better generalization of FBP models, all models were trained on the SCUT-FBP5500 dataset and tested on all datasets for 5 trials. Please refer to section 3.4.1 for the explanation. We also revised the paper with more details.

The inconsistency of FB standards between datasets could be considered as the domain shift. To address this problem, existing methods must learn the invariant from all datasets. Instead, we expect to learn the relative order of FB from a single dataset which has a better generalization across datasets. They are very different. Please refer to the paper on page 2, lines 3-7.

Thanks for recommending the model proposed by F. Bougourzi et al. We retrained their released code, tested it on all datasets, and report the results below, which are also included in the paper. One can see UOL is slightly inferior to their model in terms of PC on the SCUT-FBP5500, but better in terms of MAE and RMSE.

content.title: Response to Reviewer 6B4M Part 3
content.comment:
**Q6. The argument based on Thurstone's theory is forced. Mainly, the theory says that when different human opinions evaluate something, there will not be unanimity, but rather a Gaussian distribution of opinions. But also, the central limit theorem says the same thing. Thurstone does not develop or prove the theory for multidimensional processes, nor that VGG features for face beauty should be Gaussian.**

A6: Our UOL uses VGG to encode the mean and variance of the distribution of ratings, other than the distribution itself. We were inspired by Thurston's theory and then designed the UOL.
Moreover, there is a psychological work has extended Thurston's theory to multidimensional spaces: 

A MULTI-DIMENSIONAL ANALOGY TO THURSTONE'S LAW OF COMPARATIVE JUDGMENT.

COHEN, HARVEY SPENCER.   University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign ProQuest Dissertations Publishing, 1973. 7411986.


**Q7. The databases do not have acceptance from the persons to be made public. Also, the paper does not discuss any concerns about the intrusiveness of the theme and potential harmful application.**

A7: All datasets used in this work are public datasets whose licenses are under applicable law. 

Thanks for your suggestion. We have included following statement into the revision in **green** color:

“The improper use of FBP models might result in an unethical impact. Devising better data forensics approaches could be countermeasures.”

content.title: After rebuttal review
content.comment:
I have read carefully the response provided to my initial concern, as well as other reviewers' opinion and the responses. Overall I am still not convinced that the paper is strong enough to be accepted and furthermore I did no improve my rating. The following issues still persist:
 - citation of prior work is uneven - many old related works cited but not discussed, while difference to recent ones is stated but less convincingly. The argument that learning "different" is not anticipated from learning to rank (in prior work) is not so strong in my view.
 - the results are not strong since this method is built to generalize better on databases different from the one used for training but behaves only marginally better than methods built for good results on a single database

So, the paper is marginally improved on the theoretically part (technical innovation), slightly better on the performance and applied to a niche, lead me to starting conclusion, which is that the paper is not a good fit for ICLR. Anyway the paper has value and if not accepted here, I strongly encourage a rearrangement and re-submission to the next venue.

content.title: Response to Reviewer T8Rk
content.comment:
Thanks for your comment. The responses to the comments are listed one by one below.

**Q1. The use of uncertainty is very similar to previous uncertainty-related methods.**

A1: Thanks for raising this point. We have included the comparison with these methods in the revision in **blue** color. Probout [1] replaces the intermediate activations with low-dimensional Gaussian distributions by adjusting the activation function, and obtains uncertainty in a lightweight manner instead of traditional Bayesian approaches. GP-DNNOR [2] considers the image quality as a distribution rather than a feature point, then models the uncertainty by a low-dimensional Gaussian distribution. However, low-dimensional Gaussian distribution naturally limits the feature expressiveness. DUL [3] and POEs [4] also model facial images as multi-dimensional Gaussian distributions, but the uncertainty is introduced to reduce the effect of the inherent noise in the image on the learning of data embedding, so only the "mean" features are used in the inferential phase. Also, the information bottleneck loss in POEs only ensures that the covariance matrix of distribution is close to the Identity matrix I. Instead, the uncertainty in our UOL is the inconsistency of human cognition, which is different from the Identity matrix. So, we expect that the FB distribution to be close to the discriminal dispersion of human rating, and then take the variance of multiple ratings as the uncertainty to constrain the distribution. Both our motivation and modeling approach have differences from other methods. Actually, we knew these works but excluded them from the paper due to the 9-page limit. 

**Q2. The FP appearance of three images in Figure 1 (a).**

A2: It is an interesting question. In our experiment, many volunteers ranked the right face as the most beautiful one, and the left face as the second one. The inconsistency between you and our volunteers is an example of the inconsistency of human cognition pointed out in this work.

**Q3. It seems that the provided images in Figure 5 have many noises.**

A3: Can you please specify what the “noises” are? The signal noise in the image, or the label (FB score) noises? If it is the signal noise, all images in this study come from datasets without any modification. If it is the label noise, the FB scores are also from datasets.

**Q4. The meaning of the predictions.**

A4: Our UOL model aims to learn a robust FB order between facial images. In FBP tasks, many methods focus on the MAE and RMSE of FB score prediction. In order to compare with these methods, we transferred the FB order to FB scores using the MC rules. Yes, a more accurate prediction of the model indicates a better representation of the trend of certain volunteers. On the contrary, FB order is more general and robust. Thus, UOL demonstrates a better PC in the experiments.



[1]. Gast, J., Roth, S.: Lightweight probabilistic deep networks. In: CVPR. (2018)

[2]. Liu, Y., Wang, F., Kong, A.W.K.: Probabilistic deep ordinal regression based on gaussian processes. In: ICCV. (2019)

[3]. Chang, J., Lan, Z., Cheng, C., Wei, Y.: Data uncertainty learning in face recognition. In: CVPR. (2020)

[4]. Li, W., Huang, X., Lu, J., Feng, J., Zhou, J.: Learning probabilistic ordinal embeddings for uncertainty-aware regression. In: CVPR. (2021)

content.title: Paper Decision
content.metareview:_summary,_strengths_and_weakn:
This paper targets at improving the generalisation performance of face beauty score prediction methods. The key insight is the poor generalization performance is from the inconsistency of beauty assessment across different datasets and persons. Thus this paper proposes to model this as an order prediction problems instead of a score regression problem. Experiments on several datasets are conducted to validate effectiveness of the proposed method. 

Strength
- this work is well motivated. 
- the presentation is clear and the paper is easy to follow.

Weakness
- The proposed method has limited novelty. It is similar to existing uncertainty-aware learning methods. 
- The proposed method does not show significantly stronger generalization performance than existing methods. This work targets at improving the generalization, but its effectiveness is not well supported by the experiments.
content.justification_for_why_not_higher_score: This paper got mixed ratings: 3 borderline ratings and 1 reject. The reviewers giving positive ratings do not give very strong evidence for supporting accept. However, the reviewers having negative opinions raise several concerns on the method novelty (comparison with exiting works) and experiments results (the improvement is not significant). The authors do respond to these concerns and the reviewers are not convinced. AC read the submission and has similar concerns.
